svg.aria-label: Queen 2.3.0 and Kafka 4.3.1 with a consumer group and with a share group at 3 million messages a second of 256-byte messages on the same three GCP brokers: p99 end-to-end latency and broker CPU against the partition count from 10 to 10 million

svg.text: Three c4-standard-24-lssd brokers (24 vCPU, 88 GB, four local NVMe disks in RAID0)

text.font-family: 'Inter Variable', Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.aria-label: p99 end-to-end latency at 3,000,000 msg/s against the partition count (log scale): Queen 2.3.0, Kafka 4.3.1 with a consumer group and Kafka 4.3.1 with a share group. Queen reads 76 ms at 10 partitions, 54 at 100, 47 at 1,000, 61 at 10,000, 53 at 100,000, 42 at 1,000,000 and 46 at 10,000,000. Kafka with a consumer group reads 11, 7.5, 8.1 and 21 ms from 10 to 10,000 partitions and 105 at 25,000. Kafka with a share group reads 9.3 ms at 100 partitions, 23 at 1,000 and 163 at 10,000.
svg.font-family: "Inter Variable", Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif

svg.aria-label: Cores used by the three brokers together at 3,000,000 msg/s against the partition count (log scale). Queen uses 18.6 cores at 10 partitions and 22.4 to 23.4 from 100 to 10,000,000. Kafka with a consumer group uses 14.9 at 10, 18.5 at 100, 21.0 at 1,000, 52.8 at 10,000 and 57.0 at 25,000, and does not carry 50,000 or 100,000. Kafka with a share group uses 24.6 at 100, 35.0 at 1,000 and 52.2 at 10,000.
